title: What the Archive Heard
paragraphs: Archives present themselves as neutral storehouses, places where the past simply waits to be consulted. The image is comforting and misleading. Every archive is the residue of earlier decisions about what was worth writing down, what was worth keeping, and who was entitled to do either, so its gaps are not accidents of time so much as traces of power.

The Haitian anthropologist Michel-Rolph Trouillot gave this intuition a precise form. In Silencing the Past, published in nineteen ninety five, he argued that silences enter history at several distinct moments, including when sources are created and when they are assembled into archives. The scheme matters because it denies historians an easy alibi. A gap cannot be blamed solely on careless clerks or lost boxes if it was already built into what the clerks were asked to record.

His own central example was the Haitian Revolution, which, he argued, Western observers at the time found hard to conceive within the categories available to them: a successful uprising of enslaved people did not fit those categories. The silence, on this account, was not simply imposed afterwards by forgetful historians. It could already lie in the documents themselves, written into the vocabulary of the people producing them.

It would be easy to draw a romantic conclusion from this, namely that the truly important past is whatever the archive omits. That conclusion is as careless as the naivety it replaces. An absence is not evidence of anything in particular until a historian can show what pressures produced it, and reading against the grain of a document still requires reading the document closely. Silence has to be argued for, not merely invoked.

What the archive offers, then, is neither a transparent window nor a wall of lies but a record of who was listening, and to whom. Treating it that way makes history harder to write and considerably more honest.

sources.claim: Michel-Rolph Trouillot Haitili bir antropologdur ve 1995'te Silencing the Past: Power and the Production of History kitabını yayımlamıştır.

Trouillot'ya göre sessizlikler tarihe birkaç ayrı anda girer; bunlar arasında kaynakların yaratılması ve arşivlerin oluşturulması vardır; kitabın merkezi örneği, dönemin Batılı gözlemcilerinin mevcut kategoriler içinde tasavvur etmekte zorlandığı Haiti Devrimi'dir.
